definitions.gloss: service, loyal service, devotion to a master or lord
definitions.explanation: Serving a lord, master, or the public with loyalty and dedication. In historical contexts, refers to the service rendered by samurai to their feudal lords.

definitions.gloss: apprenticeship, working as a live-in servant
definitions.explanation: Working in a household or business as a live-in worker, typically starting from a young age. A common practice in pre-modern and early modern Japan.

examples.japanese: {武士|ぶし}は{主君|しゅくん}に{奉公|ほうこう}した。
{御恩|ごおん}と{奉公|ほうこう}は{封建|ほうけん}{制度|せいど}の{基本|きほん}だった。
examples.english: Favor and service were the foundation of the feudal system.

examples.japanese: {滅私|めっし}{奉公|ほうこう}の{精神|せいしん}で{働|はたら}く。
examples.english: To work with a spirit of selfless devotion.

examples.japanese: 12{歳|さい}で{商家|しょうか}に{奉公|ほうこう}に{出|で}た。
examples.english: At age 12, he was sent to work as an apprentice at a merchant house.

examples.japanese: {丁稚|でっち}{奉公|ほうこう}は{厳|きび}しい{修行|しゅぎょう}だった。
examples.english: Working as an apprentice was harsh training.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}、{呉服屋|ごふくや}に{奉公|ほうこう}して{商売|しょうばい}を{学|まな}んだ。
examples.english: My grandfather apprenticed at a kimono shop when he was young and learned the trade.

notes:
USAGE:
Most commonly encountered in historical and cultural contexts. The compound {滅私|めっし}{奉公|ほうこう} (selfless devotion/service) is still used in modern Japanese, though sometimes with a critical nuance suggesting excessive self-sacrifice for an organization.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {滅私|めっし}{奉公|ほうこう}: selfless devotion
- {丁稚|でっち}{奉公|ほうこう}: apprenticeship (especially in a merchant house)
- {御恩|ごおん}と{奉公|ほうこう}: favor and service (feudal reciprocity)
- {奉公|ほうこう}に{出|で}る: to go into service/apprenticeship

ETYMOLOGY:
The {御恩|ごおん}と{奉公|ほうこう} system was the mutual obligation between lords and vassals in medieval Japan: lords granted land ({御恩|ごおん}) and vassals provided military service ({奉公|ほうこう}).
